articles.note: Corrected title is natural Russian and accurately frames both objects as sharing a sky area. The ESO claim is explicitly dated to 1999 rather than presented as a final current conclusion. The 2011 HST source accurately supports the added blue central population and ongoing-star-formation statement. The qualified Local Group-edge wording, projection explanation, target binding, self-check, source count and word range pass.

checked_sources.evidence: IAU table lists Antlia/Ant and Apus/Aps; significance text explains the original star patterns generally have no physical connection and are perspective effects.
ESO identifies NGC 2997 as an Antlia spiral roughly 30 million light-years away, brightest member of its namesake group, imaged in infrared with VLT HAWK-I.
The dated 27-Feb-1999 ESO report calls Antlia dwarf an outlying Local Group member and describes its then-inferred old-dominated population plus central H I.

2011 HST-based abstract calls Antlia at the Local Group edge and finds an appreciable blue central population confirming ongoing star formation; this materially qualifies the undated 1999-era description.
2013 study identifies Antlia among original NGC 3109 association members; it does not negate its Local Group-edge wording.
2015 Antlia B paper explicitly distinguishes Antlia B from the original Antlia dwarf and calls the original another likely NGC 3109 satellite.
NASA identifies NGC 6101 as loosely packed globular cluster in Apus at roughly 50,000 light-years, with Hubble multiwavelength observations to characterize its populations.
ESA/Hubble 2014 report says IC 4499 is a Milky Way globular in Apus, roughly 12 billion years old, and at that time found no sign of multiple generations.
2018 primary abstract reports the first detection of multiple populations in IC 4499: two sub-populations with different nitrogen abundance.

articles.note: Exact object hash is unchanged from the preceding review. Prior opened-source checks remain valid: NGC 6101 identity/distance/loose structure and IC 4499's 2014-era non-detection versus 2018 nitrogen-population finding are accurately time-bounded.
